newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Fighting rocks Tajikistan on eve of peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Fighting rocks Tajikistan on eve of peace talks.

text.p: Islamist rebels clashed with government troops in Tajikistan on Sunday only a day before planned peace talks in neighbouring Afghanistan between the leaders of the warring sides, Interfax news agency said.

The Russian news agency quoted unnamed military sources as saying that opposition fighters had driven back government forces late on Saturday from the disputed town of Tavildara, 200 km (120 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe.
The agency said sporadic fighting continued on Sunday.
Officials in Dushanbe were not immediately available for comment.

The town, the subject of bitter clashes for nearly a year, straddles a strategically important road linking the mountainous eastern half of the former Soviet republic, largely controlled by the guerrillas, to the government-controlled west.

A series of battles have raged in the last few days over several remote towns east of Dushanbe in what diplomats say is an attempt by the warring sides to beef up their bargaining positions at the negotiation table on Monday.
The latest fighting came on the eve of talks planned between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and rebel leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri at an undisclosed location in northern Afghanistan.

But the government said on Sunday talks with Nuri -- apparently forced down in a United Nations aircraft on Saturday by jets belonging to Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia on the way to the negotiations -- would still take place.
"Rakhmonov will go to Afghanistan tomorrow," Tajik presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov said on Sunday.
A Taleban spokesman in western Afghanistan said the aircraft, reported by Iranian radio to be carrying Nuri, had been released and allowed to fly on to Kunduz in northern Afghanistan.

Tens of thousands have been killed and many more made homeless in Tajikistan's bloody four-year civil war where seething regional and clan rivalries underly the conflict between the Islamist rebels and the secular government.
A United Nations-sponsored ceasefire confirmed last July is routinely flouted.
